log.hypothesis: Baseline with the unedited model: E_ref=1 by definition; I expect the reference to equal the original on clean jets (e_clean ~0).
Reference on clean/soft/P jets and a photon pT-fraction scan; expect ref(soft)=orig(clean) below a threshold between 1e-3 and 3e-3 of jet pT, and ref=orig above.
Original logits on the same constructed set, to compare with the reference row by row.

Map the drop rule per pid: one particle added to jets whose original clean logits I have; dropped iff ref equals orig(clean). Expect photons dropped iff pt<0.8 and E<~1.8 GeV, neutral hadrons iff E<~2.2 GeV, charged never (or only far below clean support pt 0.135).
Capture clean and soft1e-3 versions of 128 jets to locate dead block-0 MLP units (reusable as a detector) and to see how the soft photon token and its neighbours differ.
Residual streams (inputs of blocks 1-4) on 64 clean + 32 soft1e-3 jets, to compute per-head queries and test whether one saturated sign pattern can suppress a token as key everywhere.
Same, blocks 5-8 inputs.
Same, blocks 9-11 inputs and the final body output (classifier keys/queries).
Classifier block-1 queries, last body block, and block-0 MLP preactivations.
Block-0 MLP input (via fc1 preactivations) for 3072 inserted photons/neutral hadrons spanning the drop boundary plus clean tokens, to fit a linear drop detector.

Two repurposed dead block-0 MLP units detect (photon and pT<0.8) or (neutral hadron and E<2.2) and write a huge saturating sign vector chosen so the token key is ignored by nearly all queries; this should remove most of the soft-photon response, leaving kNN-neighbour contamination.
Per-jet E1 errors on clean/soft/P/scan rows to locate the residual error (expect P jets with many dropped photons and near-threshold photons to dominate).

Block-0 MLP inputs for clean and hand-noised jets (t=0.2,0.5,0.85; block-0 inputs do not depend on the time token) to choose quiet channels whose content stays within +-1.5 also under noise, and to measure old-row preactivation ranges of dead units.

Sparse binary circuit: exact pT/E steps (embed MLP), pid markers, constant-shifted readout channels with exact cancellers, AND-detector writing the same saturating kill vector, and a time-token gate through the dead block-0 attention so nothing fires in generation. Expect E_ref slightly better than E1 (exact AND), clean/J side effects ~0, and gen_drift near 0.

Adding a block-4 flip unit that re-patterns the killed token to a sign vector optimised for blocks 5-11 and the classifier heads (predicted attention leakage halves in blocks 5-11 and drops 7x in the classifier) should lower the ~0.012 S per-dropped-particle floor.
Per-jet E3 errors to see why P lags: expect error to grow with the number of dropped particles and to be near zero for P jets without drops.

Robustness of E3 across particle types: dropped photons/neutral hadrons should show the ~0.01 S floor; kept photons, kept neutral hadrons and all charged insertions should match the reference (=original) to ~1e-3.

Diagnose the worst dropped-photon cases of E3 on B: either a binary read fails (detector pre-activation not saturated, so no kill) or the kill fires and something else leaks. I expect detector pre >= 50 for the good cases and a failed read on some bad ones.

Pairs (B jet with killed photon, its clean base jet) under E3: locate the block where the other tokens start to differ. If block0 already differs, the path is kNN/local features; if block1, the interaction bias lets the killed token be attended.
E3 with 10x sharper embed steps (k=2e4): fewer partially-cancelled markers near thresholds, so clean/gen residuals shrink; E_ref about unchanged.
Sparse kill vector on 256 most key-relevant channels with a re-optimised pattern, no flip: about half the kill DoF; predicted leakage similar to dense s4 so E_ref near E2.
Sparse kill vector on 128 channels: smaller edit, more leakage; E_ref somewhat worse.
Sparse kill on 192 channels (re-optimised pattern).
Sparse kill on 320 channels; between S256 and dense.
Sparse kill on 384 channels.
S256 plus a block-4 flip of 48 channels (pattern optimised for blocks 5-11 and classifier within the 256-channel support); predicted leakage in late blocks drops 0.57->0.44.
Paired soft1e-4/clean jets under S192: locate in which blocks the summary and particle tokens start to deviate (leakage entry points) to explain why sparse kill beats dense.
Paired soft1e-4/clean jets under E4: locate in which blocks the summary and particle tokens start to deviate (leakage entry points) to explain why sparse kill beats dense.

Kill support chosen by key-gain per value-damage (23% less value perturbation than S192 at similar key suppression); if value damage under interaction-bias-driven attention drives the residual error, E_ref improves over S192.
Same value-aware support with 256 channels.

S192 plus an interaction-MLP unit giving a -40*GELU bias to every particle pair whose softer member has pT<0.12 GeV (below every clean particle, always in the drop set). If out-of-distribution pair biases let the soft1e-4 photon be attended despite key suppression, e_soft1e-4 should drop clearly; soft1e-3 and P unchanged; small gen drift from rare noised ultra-soft tokens.

P jets vs the same jets with dropped particles removed (exact reference input) under S192i: separate kNN contamination (block-0 diffs of kept particles) from attention leakage (block-1 attention-output diffs) and the total summary-token deviation.
S192 + interaction kill with threshold 0.10 GeV (still covers all soft1e-4 photons, 0.05-0.085 GeV): same E_ref as S192i, about half the t=0.85 generator drift.
Small variant: 128-channel kill + interaction kill (0.10 GeV).
Final-small candidate = S128 with the embed step units keeping their old (irrelevant) fc1 entries: identical behaviour to S128, 9 fewer DoF.
Final-mid candidate = S192 with trimmed embed fc1 edits: same as S192 (E_ref 0.081), 9 fewer DoF.
Final-large candidate = F192 + interaction-MLP pair kill below 0.12 GeV: same as S192i (E_ref 0.0756).

Unseen probe types (soft neutral hadron 1e-3/1e-4, two photons at 3e-4, collinear photon at 5e-4 next to the hardest particle): reference should equal the original on the clean jet whenever the inserted particles satisfy the drop rule.
Original logits on the unseen probe set (denominator of the ratio).
F192 on unseen probes: ratios similar to visible soft probes (0.02-0.06), collinear case closer to P (kNN, ~0.15).
F192i on unseen probes: like F192 but better on the 1e-4 neutral hadron (pair kill below 0.12 GeV).
F128 on unseen probes: roughly 2-3x the F192 ratios.

Controls for the construction gap: practice soft1e-3 rows; my recipe photon at 1e-3; practice kinematics relabelled pid 7; practice photon moved to a random position. Reference should drop the particle in (nearly) all rows.

If the gap is construction-specific, the practice block gives ~0.008 and one of the other blocks reproduces ~0.03; I expect the pid-7 relabel to be similar to practice and the moved/my-recipe photons to be worse.
